debt_ceiling.note: Raise sites whose category is bookkeeping-debt. The ceiling only falls: re-categorize a site with a written reason, or fix it.

categorized_raises.note: Raises in a lifecycle or operation path that predate the rule that they use SecurityRefusalError, InvalidRequestError or UnknownOutcomeError. A module's count and the ceiling only fall: convert a raise to a categorized type, then lower the count.

operator_waits.trigger: recovery owner projection of a Job already in waiting-for-operator
operator_waits.advertised_action: inherits the job: resume/retire when eligible
operator_waits.reason: Read-side projection of an existing Job state onto a typed owner view; it creates no wait.
Success path reported as waiting; give it its own non-operator state.

operator_waits.trigger: workload stop or local cleanup unconfirmed
operator_waits.advertised_action: automatic: the typed unknown outcome (wait reason stop-unconfirmed or cleanup-unconfirmed) is retried by the Controller after the exact-resume inspection
operator_waits.irreversible_effect: workload may still hold GPU memory; Stop is idempotent
operator_waits.reason: Stop is idempotent and restart-safe: the unknown outcome carries a typed wait reason, and the Controller retries it instead of parking it.

operator_waits.trigger: container runtime stop or stop metadata unconfirmed
operator_waits.advertised_action: automatic: typed unknown outcome with evidence (wait reason stop-unconfirmed or stop-metadata-unconfirmed), retried by the Controller after observing
operator_waits.irreversible_effect: container may still run; re-stop is idempotent
operator_waits.reason: Stop and uninstall are idempotent: the Controller treats any waiting result as an uncertain effect and retries after observing.

operator_waits.trigger: controller cancellation could not stop the active job / runtime state uncertain
cancelled workload model custody (installation ACL transition) unconfirmed
operator_waits.advertised_action: automatic: typed unknown outcome with evidence (wait reason model-custody-unconfirmed), retried by the Controller after observing
operator_waits.irreversible_effect: ACL on shared model files may stay granted
operator_waits.reason: finish_installation_acl_transition is an idempotent local step: the agent repeats it (bounded, three retries on transient storage errors) and only a persistent failure reports unknown with evidence (stage model-custody, error category) for the Controller to observe.

operation_kinds: every operation running at agent restart
operator_waits.trigger: agent restarted with an operation in progress
operator_waits.advertised_action: automatic for restart-safe kinds: typed unknown outcome (wait reason agent-restart-interrupted)
operator_waits.reason: Already typed as an unknown outcome with a closed wait reason; recipe.job.run.v1 and recipe.build.v1 remain parked (see their entries).

operator_waits.trigger: the core decided backoff (an automatic retry) or a queued retry; projected onto the stored vocabulary
operator_waits.advertised_action: automatic: next_action_at schedules the claim (the Spark polls; the label waiting-for-operator is legacy)
operator_waits.irreversible_effect: none: only a restart-safe or fenced order is ever scheduled (core rule 1)
operator_waits.reason: Projection of a core decision. The stored label is kept for compatibility; no operator is involved and the order is claimable when next_action_at is due.

operator_waits.trigger: the core decided observing or needs-operator for an irreversible order (a user job or a build) whose effect cannot be observed from the Controller
operator_waits.advertised_action: resume/retire (operator_resume_candidates_in_session) while the order is eligible; otherwise the reconciler re-evaluates the wait on every pass and ends it when its job ends or is cancelled
operator_waits.irreversible_effect: a user job may have run or still be running; a build may have produced output
operator_waits.reason: Core rule 3: needs-operator only for an irreversible order with an advertised action. Without one the order keeps being re-evaluated and a cancel ends it with its effect recorded as unknown.

operator_waits.trigger: an agent-upgrade helper acknowledgement (or failure) the owner finds is not proof of the target build
operator_waits.advertised_action: automatic: the core schedules the fenced retry in the same call (schedule_agent_upgrade_retry)
operator_waits.irreversible_effect: none: the claim refuses to install over any binary but the exact rollback source
operator_waits.reason: The order is reopened and immediately decided by the core, which retries it behind the dpkg safety fence; it never stays waiting.

operator_waits.trigger: every order of a parent job has finished and at least one waits
operator_waits.advertised_action: inherits the waiting child: automatic retry, or resume/retire when eligible
operator_waits.reason: Pure projection of the children onto the parent job; allowed exactly while a child wait is allowed.

operator_waits.trigger: the job's order is parked for an operator (its effect is unknown after the observation budget) and no cancel is requested
operator_waits.advertised_action: stop: ArtifactJobAdapter.actions; the cancel endpoint takes it (a waiting parent accepts it) and the job's supported_actions advertises it
operator_waits.irreversible_effect: the job process may still be running and holding GPU/memory
operator_waits.reason: Irreversible and uncertain (audit C8, now FIX-ACTION done: Stop is advertised and accepted). The row is a projection of the order's core decision (rule 3). The job never waits on its own: a requested cancel is shown as cancelling and ends cancelled with the effect unknown and a residue record (rule 4), and the API contract refuses waiting-for-operator without supported_actions=[stop].

Audit notes: Authenticated attempt fence, lease and certificate checks: a stale or foreign attempt must not mutate state.

A malformed, stale, replayed or superseded user request or reviewed plan, refused at submit time (request-led). Audit notes: User job submission validated against the recipe artifact contract.

Bookkeeping uncertainty (missing receipt, stale stored plan, persisted state, changed scope) that rule 5 of the lifecycle core turns into unknown-then-reconcile. Debt: the ceiling only falls. Audit notes: Stored artifact-job evidence/plan consistency.

Fail closed by design: authentication, authorization, signature, digest at ingress, path or secret safety, fence authority, or a destructive-effect owner guard. Audit notes: Deletion guard: when ownership or references are unknown the object is kept (fail closed for destructive effects only).

Fail closed by design: authentication, authorization, signature, digest at ingress, path or secret safety, fence authority, or a destructive-effect owner guard. Audit notes: Deletion guard: when ownership or references are unknown the object is kept (fail closed for destructive effects only). Ingress digest/size verification of downloaded bytes and manifest identity (verified once, at ingress). Download source trust: allowed hosts, redirect refusal, credentials, filesystem path safety.

A malformed, stale, replayed or superseded user request or reviewed plan, refused at submit time (request-led). Audit notes: Malformed, replayed or stale user request (key reuse, cursor, selector, pin, cancel).

Admission or capacity busy and provider-transient errors that carry a retry; the owner retries them. Audit notes: (step 4) a missing or unverified object receipt is unknown, not final: the raise now names recovery=reverify with a retry hint, re-verifies the set (heals the row from the receipts, or queues one download of the missing objects), and the consumer's retry succeeds once it is done; the refusal ends nothing. Earlier notes: Carries recovery/retry_after metadata and is already retried by the download worker.

Artifact identity and source trust validated before any byte is fetched or served: the digest and size pins that ingress verification relies on must exist, relative paths cannot traverse (no '..', no absolute or backslash path, no NUL), sources must be an allowed scheme with no credentials, the canonical huggingface.co or GitHub API authority, and a mutable (non-pinned) revision is never accepted. Fail closed by design: bytes without a verifiable pin are never downloaded. Damaged persisted copies never reach these checks as a blocker: stored manifests are read through read_or_rebuild.

Destructive-effect owner guard: removal reservation fences (fence authority) and the in-use refusal of a model removal. Fail closed for destructive effects only: when ownership or references are unknown the object is kept, and the refusal carries recovery=retry where the cause is transient. A changed scope after planning is not here: it defers the removal (unknown, retried by the lifecycle core).

The Controller-to-agent serving seam: only a file the set's manifest lists, under a validated relative path and exact digests, is served. A path, digest or (object, path) pair the manifest does not list is refused (path safety, no caller-controlled filesystem path).

A request names an identity the cache or catalog does not hold (operation id, cache entry, selector, recipe revision, model pin, variant): the defined answer is the 404/422 of that request, which its caller (API route, distribution, run/switch, image availability) already translates. Nothing is blocked or stranded: the identity is requested again (download, catalog sync) request-led. Worker-internal lookups of a vanished row return and skip instead (unknown, rule 5); and an entry whose stored manifest is unreadable is rebuilt or listed as unknown. Not convertible without editing in-flight distribution and image-availability callers that rely on NotFound.

A malformed or contradictory user request at submit time: a manifest document or write-side envelope that does not satisfy the contract, pins that disagree with each other or with the requested artifact-set identity, an access recheck on an operation that is not in the terminal access-failure state. Refused when the request is accepted, never while reading stored state.

A provider transfer failure (HTTP error, unreachable source, GitHub release transfer) raised with recovery=resume and a retry hint: the transfer boundary (_finish_failed) reports it as a retryable outcome and the lifecycle core reschedules the exact transfer with bounded backoff, resuming the retained bytes. The owner retries it; it never reaches an operator.
A malformed, stale, replayed or superseded user request or reviewed plan, refused at submit time (request-led). Audit notes: Malformed/replayed/stale user request.

Admission or capacity busy and provider-transient errors that carry a retry; the owner retries them. Audit notes: Admission busy: retried by the owning worker (Run/Switch hold, profile admission retry).

Bookkeeping uncertainty (missing receipt, stale stored plan, persisted state, changed scope) that rule 5 of the lifecycle core turns into unknown-then-reconcile. Debt: the ceiling only falls. Audit notes: Evidence/owner/scope bookkeeping on result projection, Stop authority, JobRun Stop, build cleanup. Installation/plan/reconciliation bookkeeping that blocks Install/Start (e.g. complete without a receipt).

Fail closed by design: authentication, authorization, signature, digest at ingress, path or secret safety, fence authority, or a destructive-effect owner guard. Audit notes: Digest/layout verification of the runtime image and artifact receipts, and the NAS-eviction prohibition.

A malformed, stale, replayed or superseded user request or reviewed plan, refused at submit time (request-led). Audit notes: Apply/cancel/retry request is stale, replayed, superseded or blocked by a reviewed plan.
Admission or capacity busy and provider-transient errors that carry a retry; the owner retries them.

Raised on the phase-advance path of a Run/Switch operation. A conflict that is not a reviewed security edge is caught at the phase checkpoint (fail -> the lifecycle core's bounded backoff, the same idempotent phase entered again) or, outside it, by the tick guard (_hold_after_advance_failure, same clock). Bookkeeping becomes unknown, then reconcile; a final verification that cannot be observed is observed again, never declared failed. Covered by test_run_switch_lifecycle.

Raised while a request is accepted, cancelled or retried (the request key, the reviewed scope, an operation that is not in a state the request applies to). No operation is ended by it: the request is refused and the caller reads the reason. Nothing in flight dead-ends.

The bounded nonblocking claim of the shared reference fence (a kernel file lock shared with other Controller processes) ran out its 30 second budget while another process reconciles. The caller's own operation (an idempotent upload or attachment, or the reconcile sweep) is retried by its requester; nothing in flight is ended by it and no state is recorded wrong.

A malformed, stale, replayed or superseded user request or reviewed plan, refused at submit time (request-led). Audit notes: User request is stale, replayed, superseded or names an unknown recipe/profile.
Admission or capacity busy and provider-transient errors that carry a retry; the owner retries them.

A load whose preview carries a security-boundary blocker (is_security_failure: authentication, authorization, signature or digest) is refused, never parked or retried: only non-security blockers wait for current conditions (_profile_preview_is_waitable). Apply refuses at submit; the recovery path refuses the same blockers.

Exact artifact identity fence: a recovery must not silently replace the model or runtime image bound in the accepted plan (docs/engineering-principles: exact identity fails closed; an alternative must be an explicit new load). The recovery caller parks the receipt with the shown reason (profile.recovery_artifact_changed) and the identity is never re-hashed here.

Destructive-effect owner guard: a new durable selector reference to an artifact whose exact removal is in flight is serialized with that removal by the artifact lifecycle owner (ArtifactLifecycleError: gate busy, fenced for deletion, or not safely inspectable), and the save relays that fence (the same security-edge the artifact-lifecycle family carries). Nothing is stored; the save succeeds once the removal completed.

The caller addressed a receipt that cannot be retried (it is not failed or waiting, or it is not a current profile load): a malformed retry request refused at submit time with a defined 409, nothing is stored or issued. Every bookkeeping mismatch of an eligible receipt is parked or noted instead (see _decline_retry).

A profile save names a recipe that has no active catalog revision: a malformed request refused at submit time (HTTP 409 on the save). A saved profile that already names such a recipe is read, shown as needing attention and planned as profile.recipe_unavailable (waiting for the catalog sync), never refused.

Admission waits that carry their own retry: a database constraint rejection mid-admission, an artifact owner holding its gate, and a build being cancelled. apply, the roster reconciliation and the pending-admission worker all park the request (_defer_pending_application) and retry it automatically with a visible next attempt.

Refused at submit time, before anything is persisted, and the caller can change the request: the entity or argument the request names does not exist or is in a state it cannot act on, the reviewed plan or workload intent is stale or superseded, or a document this very call composes violates its contract. Raised only from the request path; damaged stored state is rebuilt from evidence or retired as unknown (lifecycle.evidence), never raised as this class.

Fence authority guarding a destructive effect: a Stop is built only from the run's exact durable Start authority, a JobRun runtime is stopped only when its exact identity matches the accepted profile Stop, and a job joins only the workload intent it was admitted under. Without that proof the Controller must not invent a destructive payload or take a newer intent, so it fails closed.

The request cannot be served yet (a collaborating service not bound, an owner busy with another operation, node or installation evidence not reported, an installation plan whose damage was retired as unknown): nothing was persisted, the typed UnknownOutcomeError tells the caller to retry, and the owner (Run/Switch phase retry, profile retry, the next preparation) does retry; the damaged row is skipped by that next preparation instead of being refused for ever.

Refused at submit time, before anything is persisted: the request intent, the package descriptor or the target list the caller sent is not an upgrade the Controller can plan, or the repair is not for its explicit Spark. Raised only from the request path (the same checks answer a replayed request); a damaged stored plan ends its rollout through _advance_rollout and is never refused as this class.

The release channel answered inconsistently (generation, signature or digest disagree while a release is being published). Nothing is persisted, the typed UnknownOutcomeError tells the caller to ask again, and a re-fetch converges once the release is complete.

The accepted operator startup deadline is a bounded budget, not stored state: its expiry ends this recovery Start and the callers fail the unfinished child operations. It never bans a fresh request: the next recovery pass derives a new deadline from the live run. Raised only at the trust boundary that enforces the retained marker.

The injected clock must be timezone-aware: a naive instant is a caller contract violation at the boundary that owns the clock, not stored bookkeeping (a stored timestamp without a zone is retired as residue before it reaches this check).

The raise is a typed retryable failure that the worker persists on the lifecycle core's bounded, jittered retry clock (RecipeImageAvailabilityService._fail, or _record_recipe_removal_failure for a removal): the evidence it names (a ModelCache plan or child, a build input, a reference that appeared during a fenced removal) is re-derived by the next attempt, so nothing waits for an operator.

A request-time refusal that carries the owner's own retry decision (retryable flag and delay) and persists nothing: a nonblocking lock that is busy, a build dependency that is being cancelled, an authority that could not be refreshed, an accepted owner row not yet readable. The caller retries with the same request key and the request reconciles against what the owner then reports.

Control flow, not a refusal: the availability execution claim was lost to a newer attempt or a cancel. _run catches it and returns without writing, and the new claim owner (or the cancel reconcile) carries the operation on, so the raise is the handoff itself.

Destructive-effect guard: a recipe cache removal and the references that compete with it are decided on one exact, reviewed scope. A review that cannot be sealed on consistent evidence, a reference scan that is unavailable (an unavailable scan does not prove an object unused), a changed scope at acceptance (reject changed effects instead of broadening consent) and an artifact reserved for removal all refuse here; the refusal names its retry or inspect action.

Rejects the shape or identity of a request before any effect: a cancellation id or reason, a digest, an action combination, a recipe revision that the request names but that is not active, a submitted identity that differs from the authoritative one, a removal plan larger than the owner document may hold. The caller fixes the request and asks again.

The request needs a collaborator this service was not wired with (the recipe metadata authority, the build executor, the ModelCache for a with-model removal): a configuration fault of the process, refused at the boundary that owns the request before any effect.

Validates the recipe document the metadata authority returned at request admission, before the operation is accepted. A stored copy never reaches this check damaged: the worker rebuilds it from the catalog revision under the digest the operation was accepted with (RecipeImageAvailabilityService._stored_recipe).

The builder's typed admission refusal (no fresh inventory, missing capability, not enough disk or memory, an unknown, incompatible or changed builder node). availability_production consumes every one of these codes (_BUILDER_ADMISSION_CODES): dispatch skips to the next builder candidate or defers the operation as the retryable recipe_image.build_capacity_wait with the refusal as its visible blocker and resume action, so the shortage waits for capacity instead of failing the build.

Exact-identity fence and ingress check: a build result is accepted only for the exact inputs it was planned under and never over different or failed evidence (digest formats are verified at ingress), and a reservation or resolution is accepted only while the recipe revision still has the content digest it was planned for. A changed identity refuses instead of substituting a different recipe or image into a bound plan; the next request replans.
Rejects a request that names a revision which is not an active recipe (nothing resolved to check or build) before any effect; the caller names the current revision and asks again.

Validates what the recipe declares against the build contract before any effect: declared build resources and security, the per-node image size, the Dockerfile the verified source bundle must carry, the runtime adapter for its engine and topology. Retrying cannot change the answer; only a new recipe revision does.
Rejects a capacity reservation whose arithmetic violates the reservation contract (a ValueError from the reservation helpers) before any reservation row is written; a caller defect, not stored state.

A typed retryable failure of managed image storage (the layered store cannot be read, the publication lock or receipt cannot be written, another owner holds the publication, the image is not yet present, a newer Controller's receipt must stay in place). The worker persists it on the lifecycle core's bounded retry clock and the next attempt re-reads the storage, so nothing waits for an operator. Every raise of these codes carries retryable=True.

Exact-image verification before publication: a receipt is published only for the stored image it names, at the size it records (never over other bytes), and an image is accepted only with the platform and runtime-interface label the recipe declares. A mismatch refuses instead of publishing or substituting a different image; archive_mismatch is already the typed re-download signal of the failure classification.

Rejects an argument or document that does not satisfy the function's contract before any effect: an exact SHA-256 or image digest, a recipe document, a runtime projection with architecture and interface, the build receipt a caller passes to prepare an image, the evidence a transport returns. The caller fixes the input; nothing is read from stored state here.

Destructive-effect fence: a profile Stop acts on a running workload, and ProfileStopAuthorityError is a SecurityRefusalError. The Stop is dispatched only when the accepted profile, its reviewed child, the run generation and the fleet intent still match the Stop exactly; when any of them has moved or cannot be established, the Controller does not stop, and the owning profile application re-derives its authority and issues a fresh Stop.

A busy or cancelling build is a retry handoff: both raises carry retryable=True. Availability preparation and the Fleet profile admission turn it into a retryable wait that their owners retry (FleetProfileAdmissionEffectBusy, a retryable availability error), and a cancel or retry request surfaces the same wait as a request-led retry once the build settles.
